import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import re
import os
import unicodedata
from collections import defaultdict, Counter
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")


def normalize_unicode(text):
    """Apply NFKC normalization to handle Unicode compatibility characters."""
    if pd.isna(text):
        return ""
    return unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", str(text))


def infer_class_for_numeric_token(token_norm):
    """Infer the most probable semantic class for a numeric token based on format patterns."""
    if not re.match(r"^\d+$", token_norm):
        return None

    # Ordinal pattern: ends with st, nd, rd, th (after removing possible suffixes)
    if (
        re.search(r"(1\d|0?[1-9])(st|nd|rd|th)$", token_norm)
        or re.search(
            r"(?<![0-9])([1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-1])(st|nd|rd|th)\b", token_norm
        )
        or token_norm.endswith(("st", "nd", "rd", "th"))
    ):
        return "ORDINAL"

    # Year pattern: exactly 4 digits starting with 19 or 20
    if len(token_norm) == 4 and token_norm[:2] in ("19", "20"):
        return "YEAR"

    # If too short for year and not ordinal, likely cardinal
    return "CARDINAL"


# Load data
train = pd.read_csv("./input/en_train.csv")
test = pd.read_csv("./input/en_test_2.csv")
sample_sub = pd.read_csv("./input/en_sample_submission_2.csv")

# Normalize before/after values in training data
train["before_norm"] = train["before"].apply(normalize_unicode)
train["after_norm"] = train["after"].apply(normalize_unicode)

# Create mapping: for each (before_norm, class), store the most frequent after_norm
token_map = defaultdict(list)
for _, row in train.iterrows():
    before = row["before_norm"]
    token_class = str(row["class"]) if pd.notna(row["class"]) else "PLAIN"
    after = row["after_norm"]
    token_map[(before, token_class)].append(after)

# Build final mapping: (before, class) -> best after
final_map = {}
for (before, token_class), afters in token_map.items():
    counter = Counter(afters)
    best_after = min(counter.keys(), key=lambda x: (-counter[x], x))
    final_map[(before, token_class)] = best_after

# Store PLAIN mappings separately (normalized keys)
plain_mapping = {}
for (before, token_class), after in final_map.items():
    if token_class == "PLAIN":
        plain_mapping[before] = after


# Enhanced rule-based normalization function with context-aware class inference
def normalize_token(token, token_class="PLAIN"):
    token_str = str(token) if pd.notna(token) else ""
    token_class_str = str(token_class) if pd.notna(token_class) else "PLAIN"

    # Apply NFKC normalization to input token
    token_norm = normalize_unicode(token_str)

    # Direct lookup first (using normalized token)
    if (token_norm, token_class_str) in final_map:
        return final_map[(token_norm, token_class_str)]

    # For PLAIN, try lowercase (normalized)
    if token_class_str == "PLAIN":
        lower_token = token_norm.lower()
        if lower_token in plain_mapping:
            return plain_mapping[lower_token]
        if token_norm in ["A", "An", "The", "a", "an", "the"]:
            return token_norm.lower()
        return token_norm

    # Rule-based fallbacks with context-aware class inference for numeric tokens
    if token_class_str in ["NUMBER", "CARDINAL", "ORDINAL", "FRACTION", "DECIMAL"]:
        if re.match(r"^\d+$", token_norm):
            # First try the original class
            if (token_norm, token_class_str) in final_map:
                return final_map[(token_norm, token_class_str)]

            # For numeric tokens not found, infer class first to avoid spurious lookups
            if token_class_str not in ["CARDINAL", "NUMBER"]:
                inferred_class = infer_class_for_numeric_token(token_norm)
                if inferred_class and (token_norm, inferred_class) in final_map:
                    return final_map[(token_norm, inferred_class)]

            # Then fallback to original class and related classes
            for cls in [
                token_class_str,
                "CARDINAL",
                "NUMBER",
                "ORDINAL",
                "FRACTION",
                "DECIMAL",
            ]:
                if cls != token_class_str and (token_norm, cls) in final_map:
                    return final_map[(token_norm, cls)]
            return token_norm

        if re.match(r"^\d+\.\d+$", token_norm):
            if (token_norm, token_class_str) in final_map:
                return final_map[(token_norm, token_class_str)]
            for cls in ["DECIMAL", "NUMBER"]:
                if (token_norm, cls) in final_map:
                    return final_map[(token_norm, cls)]
            return token_norm

    # Date rule
    if token_class_str == "DATE":
        match = re.match(r"(\d{1,2})/(\d{1,2})/(\d{2,4})", token_norm)
        if match:
            month, day, year = match.groups()
            try:
                m, d, y = int(month), int(day), int(year)
                if y < 100:
                    y = 2000 + y if y < 50 else 1900 + y
                month_names = [
                    "january",
                    "february",
                    "march",
                    "april",
                    "may",
                    "june",
                    "july",
                    "august",
                    "september",
                    "october",
                    "november",
                    "december",
                ]
                if 1 <= m <= 12:
                    return f"{month_names[m-1]} {d} {y}"
            except:
                pass
            return token_norm

    # Time rule
    if token_class_str == "TIME":
        match = re.match(r"(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})(?::(\d{2}))?", token_norm)
        if match:
            hour, minute = map(int, match.groups()[:2])
            if minute == 0:
                return f"{hour} o'clock"
            elif minute < 10:
                return f"{hour} oh {minute}"
            return f"{hour} {minute}"
        return token_norm

    # Currency rule
    if token_class_str == "MONEY":
        match = re.match(r"\$([\d,]+)(?:\.(\d{1,2}))?", token_norm)
        if match:
            dollars = match.group(1).replace(",", "")
            cents = match.group(2) if match.group(2) else "00"
            if cents == "00":
                return f"{dollars} dollars"
            return f"{dollars} dollars, {cents} cents"
        return token_norm

    # Measurement rule
    if token_class_str == "MEASURE":
        match = re.match(
            r"(\d+)(ft|lb|inches?|cm|meters?|kg|grams?)", token_norm, re.IGNORECASE
        )
        if match:
            value, unit = match.groups()
            unit_lower = unit.lower()
            unit_map = {
                "ft": "feet",
                "lb": "pounds",
                "in": "inches",
                "inch": "inches",
                "cm": "centimeters",
                "m": "meters",
                "kg": "kilograms",
                "g": "grams",
            }
            if unit_lower in unit_map:
                return f"{value} {unit_map[unit_lower]}"
        return token_norm

    # Letters rule
    if token_class_str == "LETTERS":
        if len(token_norm) == 1 and token_norm.isalpha():
            return token_norm.lower()
        return token_norm

    return token_norm
